positions.as_written: Assess landing on one leg, since two legged landings conceal asymmetry and most injuries are single leg.
Read peak knee flexion as the most informative single variable available by observation.
Expect a laboratory drop landing to underestimate the demands of a contested landing.
Assess under fatigue and on one leg, since that is nearer the injury condition.
State that frontal plane screening has not predicted injury consistently.
Expect fear of reinjury to change landing strategy, and address it as part of the assessment rather than after it.

Take the athlete's age, physiology, comorbidities, knee demand, psychological state and their own ideas, concerns and expectations into return to sport decisions, because landing confidence and landing capacity diverge.
